target.title: feat: add guarded FakeCo AWS owner
target.body:
## Summary

- add a guarded FakeCo-only CloudFormation owner for one private ARM64 ClickClack VM in the dedicated member account
- reuse an explicitly supplied, account-owned VPC, private subnet, and active egress path; allow TCP 8080 only from approved source security groups
- add protected manual plan/apply/verify/teardown operations with exact account, live template/resource inventory, network, AMI, storage, security-group, and workload-IAM replay
- add deterministic SSM bootstrap, seed equality, health/readiness, metadata-only metrics, runtime identity, SQLite backup/integrity, rollback-safe restore, and retained-data teardown proof
- document account prerequisites, Environment inputs, costs, durations, canary handoff, failure recovery, and disposal boundaries

Production Cloudflare Worker, Container, Postgres, R2, domains, release, and version paths are unchanged.

## Safety boundary

- `plan` is the default and never executes its change set
- `apply` rejects resource removals and actual or conditional replacement
- no public IP, SSH key, port 22 rule, VPC, subnet, route table, NAT gateway, load balancer, or DNS resource is created
- VPC, subnet, ingress sources, transit gateway, and every distinct NAT-managed ENI must belong to the dedicated account
- the instance role is inline-policy-only, permissions-boundary constrained, and limited to SSM plus exact artifact/log/backup/KMS destinations
- verify and teardown match the current CloudFormation template and logical-resource inventory, accept stable rollback-complete recovery, and fail closed on extra block devices or live instance, volume, security-group, IAM, release, and runtime-image drift
- teardown refreshes stack and instance evidence immediately before retention, takes a fresh hot backup and encrypted snapshot, retains the root volume and versioned manifest, and contains no implicit data-delete path
- restore uses one evidence file, a bounded health/readiness wait, and an error trap that restores and re-probes the prior database or leaves the app stopped
- workflow inputs contain identifiers only; no GitHub or application secret values are added

## Validation

Exact candidate: `184e6d75c4206cea31a82fe248a6cc8da2b06ea4` / tree `e4e036e2c1e4226b509a50e7115f83bc7b20fa51`.

Diff: 12 files, 5,053 insertions, 24 deletions; SHA-256 `db3c7fbdd64074fc3ef0a87d7e793e50f5f2eb8f7143d4b390b2729ebc1dd73c`. Source archive SHA-256: `4a0a3d23d0832bb6c1203686f4ee94d42d711042e028cfc72e79ddde3a90da4c`.

- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm docs:site`
- `pnpm coverage` — 86.5%
- `pnpm test:e2e` — 46 passed
- `pnpm test:fakeco-aws` — 29 passed, including stack/template/resource, rollback, extra-volume, runtime, cleanup, and restore mutations
- `actionlint .github/workflows/fakeco-aws.yml`
- `shellcheck deploy/fakeco/aws/bootstrap.sh` plus Bash syntax and ShellCheck proof for the extracted restore block
- `uvx --from cfn-lint cfn-lint deploy/fakeco/aws/template.json`
- exact-head Docker buildx `linux/arm64` and `linux/amd64` builds, cache-only with no registry output
- source-blind operator behavior validation — contract satisfied at confidence 0.98; deterministic private plan, credential non-persistence, wrong-region, duplicate-ingress, and overlapping-destination mutations covered
- canonical autoreview — cumulative branch findings repaired; final policy cleanup clean with no accepted/actionable findings at confidence 1.0

## Review repairs

- install the versioned official AWS CLI ARM64 archive after checksum verification instead of relying on an unavailable Noble package
- accept reserved CloudFormation `aws:` tags while rejecting every unexpected customer-owned tag
- scope remote script listing to the artifact owner prefix and bound SSM execution
- make teardown rollback-safe when a failed update leaves the prior verified release serving
- bind restore to observed runtime evidence and roll back or stop on readiness failure
- match the live template and logical-resource set before destructive workflow stages
- reject every unexpected attached volume and refresh instance evidence immediately before snapshot/deletion
- permit guarded recovery from `UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE`
- require dedicated-account ownership for the supplied network, including deduplicated NAT ENI ownership checks

Public Model Identifier Gate: **PASS**. The exact diff, source archive, tests, workflow, generated docs, cache-only build logs, and public PR proof contain zero blocking unknown identifiers. The canary uses the public ClawRouter model-ref syntax and documented example from [official OpenClaw ClawRouter documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/clawrouter).

## Live-proof waiver and residual risk

No AWS resource, GitHub Environment, secret, account, workflow dispatch, release, version, tag, or registry artifact was created while preparing or validating this PR. Authenticated member-account apply/verify/backup/restore/teardown proof remains unavailable because the service identity and protected Environment are not active.

After that exact gate was reported, the repository owner explicitly directed **“land it”** on 2026-07-11. This waives only the pre-merge live AWS lifecycle proof for this PR; it does not authorize a deployment or any account, Environment, secret, or resource creation. The manual workflow remains protected and must not be dispatched until the documented account foundation and permissions are independently available.

target.title: feat: add multi-class artifact viewer
target.body:
## Summary

- add an in-app, read-only artifact viewer for code, text, Markdown, PDF, DOCX, and uploaded HTML files
- replace document download-only cards with an accessible open action while preserving downloads and existing image/audio/video behavior
- add desktop side-pane and mobile full-screen presentation with focus restoration, Escape handling, loading states, and pane-local fallbacks
- classify using stored upload MIME metadata plus the original filename because unsafe upload types are served as `application/octet-stream`
- add the viewer dependencies, embedded production assets, documentation, and browser coverage

## Viewer behavior

- code and text render as inert escaped source; known languages up to 256 KiB are highlighted in a terminable worker, while larger files use escaped plain-text fallback
- Markdown supports sanitized preview and source modes through the existing `marked` and DOMPurify pipeline
- PDF supports one-page-at-a-time navigation, page counts, and zoom using the existing `pdfjs-dist` integration
- DOCX converts semantically in-browser with Mammoth and sanitizes the resulting HTML
- uploaded HTML is sanitized, placed in an empty-sandbox `iframe.srcdoc`, and constrained by a CSP that permits only inline styles and local `data:`/`blob:` assets
- unsupported files show metadata and a download fallback without execution

## Safety contract

- text, code, Markdown, and HTML previews are limited to 2 MiB
- syntax highlighting is isolated from the UI thread in a terminable worker with a 2-second timeout and 2 MiB output cap; files above 256 KiB remain escaped source without syntax parsing
- PDF thumbnail and viewer canvases are checked before allocation: each DPR-scaled backing dimension is capped at 8,192 pixels and the backing store at 16 megapixels, with download fallback for pages outside the policy
- DOCX conversion is limited to 16 MiB; PDF preview uses the existing 64 MiB upload ceiling
- previews use same-origin authenticated fetches, abort on close/switch, and release worker/PDF resources
- HTML scripts, forms, frames, external links/resources, and network-bearing CSS references are removed before rendering; server download headers and CSP are unchanged
- v1 is read-only and does not add artifact storage, editing, collaboration, or CRDT state
- no database, OpenAPI, SDK, or public transport contract changes

## Verification

- `pnpm check`
- `pnpm coverage` — 86.5% total Go coverage
- `pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/artifact-viewer.spec.ts` — 6 passed, covering classification, worker highlighting, near-limit escaped fallback and cancellation, Markdown source/preview, normal PDF page/zoom, PDF canvas dimension and pixel budgets, oversized-page download fallback, bounded DOCX conversion, hostile-HTML isolation, oversized/malformed fallbacks, mobile sizing, and `message.updated`
- `CAPTURE_ARTIFACT_PROOF=1 pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/artifact-viewer.spec.ts -g "opens safe code"` — 1 passed and produced live HTML-isolation diagnostics
- `CAPTURE_PDF_LIMIT_PROOF=1 pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/artifact-viewer.spec.ts -g "shows local fallbacks"` — 1 passed and produced live oversized-PDF allocation diagnostics
- production web/SDK build and embedded asset refresh completed through the E2E web server
- browser visual inspection completed for the desktop side pane, mobile full-screen layout, HTML isolation, and PDF canvas-limit fallback

## Real behavior proof

These captures come from the local OpenClaw → ClickClack delivery path and the running viewer.

### Oversized PDF canvas allocation

The crafted fixture is a small valid PDF with a 20,000 × 20,000-point page. Browser-observed diagnostics show the configured 8,192-pixel dimension ceiling and 16-megapixel budget, zero viewer canvases allocated, and the authenticated download fallback visibly available.

![Oversized PDF rejected before canvas allocation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/2bfceea847aa98afe52c281797a14dfc246e0b03/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-pdf-canvas-limit.png)

### Uploaded HTML isolation

The hostile fixture attempts script execution, form submission, nested framing, external navigation, image loading, stylesheet import, and CSS URL loading. Browser-observed diagnostics show an empty sandbox token list, an absent script marker, zero requests to the sentinel host, no scripts/forms/frames in the preview DOM, and stripped external URL references.

![Uploaded HTML isolation with live browser diagnostics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/a2460a156d7165e01322dc71d37f85996f3656c0/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-html-isolation.png)

Reproduction details: [`docs/artifact-viewer-security-proof.md`](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/blob/2bfceea847aa98afe52c281797a14dfc246e0b03/docs/artifact-viewer-security-proof.md)

### Behavior while testing PR

![Markdown preview side pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-markdown-preview.png)

![Markdown source side pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/artifact-viewer-markdown-source.png)

### Current behavior before merging PR

![OpenClaw-delivered ClickClack attachment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/openclaw-clickclack-attachment.png)

![Download control behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/clickclack/3d94e34/docs/proof/openclaw-download-permission.png)

## Out of scope

- OpenClaw `sendMedia` delivery remains a separate companion PR
- collaborative Markdown, mutable uploads, revisioned artifacts, and Jot/CRDT storage remain follow-up work
